FAQ.heading:
Before we begin,
a few answers.
FAQ.description: A few things you might be wondering before turning your idea into a project.

company.question: What kind of company is GRIDS?
company.answer: GRIDS is a software development company building websites, applications, business systems, and AI solutions. We work with you to understand your goals and everyday challenges, then turn them into useful products—from planning through development.

services.question: What can you build, and when should I get in touch?
services.answer: We build websites, online stores, web and mobile apps, CRM and admin systems, workflow automation, and AI tools that use your company’s knowledge. Get in touch when you want to launch a service, connect scattered information, or reduce repetitive work.

pricing.question: How do you determine development costs?
pricing.answer: Costs depend on the features, design scope, integrations, and timeline. We clarify the scope during consultation before providing an estimate. If you have a set budget, we can explore a phased approach that starts with your priorities.

quality.question: How do you ensure project quality?
quality.answer: We agree on the scope and review criteria upfront, then review progress and deliverables together at key stages. An 80% refund policy also applies under agreed conditions. We explain the eligibility criteria and process during consultation.

starting.question: Can I book a consultation if I only have an idea?
starting.answer: Yes. You do not need a finished brief. Tell us about the problem you want to solve, who the service is for, and any examples you have in mind. We can work through the essential features and priorities together.

support.question: What does maintenance cost after launch?
support.answer: Costs depend on the size of the service, its operating environment, and the support you need. We distinguish running costs, such as hosting, from maintenance and feature development, then agree on the support that makes sense for your business.

Pricing.title:
The right scope.
A clear price.
Pricing.description: Use these prices as a guide, not a fixed quote.
Pricing.budgetNote:
Start with your budget.
We’ll shape the scope together.
Pricing.currencyNote: All prices in KRW · VAT excluded

packages.title: Choose a scope. We’ll take it from there.
packages.description: Share your goals and materials; we’ll guide planning and production. Choose a service and compare three proposed scopes.
packages.draftNote: These proposals combine documented starting rates and add-ons. A fixed fee is confirmed after detailed scoping; these are not yet finalized selling prices.
packages.homepageNote: Choose Template, Custom or Premium for your website. Analytics starts with Custom; CMS and premium motion are included in Premium. AI video length and production scope are agreed before work begins.

scope.title: A fixed fee for an agreed scope
scope.body: Pages, features and revisions are agreed first. Requests outside that scope receive a separate quote.

costs.title: Third-party costs are separate
costs.body: Domains, hosting, API usage, payment fees and paid assets are excluded.

translation.title: Content and translations
translation.body: We review your brand materials and content during consultation. Multilingual packages assume client-supplied translations.

custom.title: Need AI, automation or a mobile app?
custom.description: AI features, standalone CRM / admin systems, automation, mobile apps, real-time features and other unpriced work require a separate scope review. Overlapping functionality is also reconciled during scoping.

rules.title: Understand what goes into the quote.
rules.description: Review base production rates and the additional work you need. These are quotation guidelines; the final proposal reflects actual scope and complexity.
rules.calculationNote: We total these components, apply the minimum engagement where relevant and review project scale and complexity to determine the final supply amount. VAT and external costs are separate.

policy.scope: Rates are not applied mechanically to every project. Actual scope and complexity take priority.
policy.information: When information is missing or scope is unclear, we clarify it before quoting. We do not guess a low fixed price.
policy.custom: Unlisted features are not assigned the price of a similar feature by assumption. They are assessed separately where needed.
policy.adjustment: Final amounts may be adjusted for project scale, complexity and proposal terms. Work beyond the initially agreed scope is quoted separately.
